title: Stream compatibility, credential cascade, and typed iterable polish across SDKs
author: Asha Nair
description: Motivation: Several customer integrations surfaced two recurring issues: (1) credential handoffs between SDKs could race during stream reconnects causing transient 401s, and (2) the async iterable/iterator ergonomics diverged between Python/TS/Go leading to inconsistent consumer patterns and duplicated adapter code. This PR unifies a compact credential cascade model, stabilizes stream resume semantics across SDKs, and polishes typed async iterables so consumers get consistent restart/resume behavior. Summary of changes: - Introduce 'CredentialCascade' abstraction (language idiomatic implementations) that attempts delegated token providers in order and exposes a single refresh hook for the runtime. - Add an idempotent session lease handshake to reduce races on reconnects; SDKs now validate lease ownership before swapping active credentials. - Normalize stream consumer interfaces: async iterators in Python, AsyncIterable in TS, and a lightweight channel iterator in Go share a documented contract for resume() and cancel(). - Backported ergonomic helpers: session_warmup(), iterable.buffered_chunks(), and a unified on_auth_failure callback surface. - Tests and migration notes included; small internal runtime change to surface session lease metadata on grpc headers. Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced (Linear ENG-1123) - [x] Python/TS/Go prototype validated against e2e streaming harness - [x] Unit + integration tests updated - [x] Manual regression run against prod-like traces - [x] Docs snippets updated (quickstarts and migration) Compatibility notes: - No public API removed; surface additions are opt-in. Consumers that previously relied on implicit token rotation may observe fewer 401 retries and different ordering of reauth attempts; this is considered a compatibility improvement. Upgrade guidance: - Pin SDKs to v1.8.x for coordinated upgrade. - Enable session_lease in config to get the full protection against credential races; defaults to off for minor-version safety. Rollback plan: revert feature flag or rollback SDK versions; runtime remains backward compatible. Related: touches SDK packages in this monorepo and coordination PRs in language repos (see linked commits).
